chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from the man: that he was asked

about a man who looked at a shepherd who urinated on a sheep. He said: 'If he recognizes it, he slaughters it and burns it. And if he does not recognize it, he divides it into two halves always until the lot falls upon it, so it is slaughtered and burned, while the rest of the flock remains safe.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a shepherd urinates on a sheep and the owner does not know which one it was?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific legal procedure for purifying a flock from the impurity (*najāsah*) of sheep urine, distinguishing between known and unknown offenders. It establishes a rigorous standard of purification where the offending sheep is not only slaughtered but its meat is burned, ensuring complete removal of the impurity, while the remainder of the flock remains pure. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on tangible purification methods in agricultural and livestock management.
